headToHead.title: Head-to-Head
headToHead.noOverlap: No shared races at this circuit.
headToHead.prompt: Select two drivers to compare their head-to-head record at this circuit.

deltaRibbon.title: Delta Ribbon
deltaRibbon.methodology: Historical time delta between {driverA} and {driverB} at {raceName}. Ribbon width = size of the gap, color = who was ahead.

circuitDetail.noData: No race data available for this circuit.

dnf.title: DNF Rate
dnf.info: How often drivers fail to finish at this circuit. High rates reveal mechanical stress, safety risks, or technically aggressive track design.
dnf.label: did not finish

poleWin.title: Pole → Win
poleWin.info: How often the pole-sitter converts to a race win. High conversion signals overtaking difficulty and front-row dominance.

gridDelta.title: Grid Δ Average
gridDelta.info: Average positions gained from starting grid to final classification, across all finishers. Positive = field typically moves forward; negative = grid order holds.
gridDelta.label: avg positions gained

streaks.title: Win Streaks
streaks.info: Longest consecutive winning runs at this circuit, by driver and by constructor. Consecutive wins across seasons signal deep track mastery.

age.title: Youngest · Oldest Winner
age.info: Age extremes among race winners at this circuit. The youngest signals a career breakthrough; the oldest, sustained elite-level performance.

natWins.title: Wins by Nationality
natWins.info: Race victories grouped by driver nationality. Reveals historical geographic dominance patterns across F1 history at this circuit.

pitStrategy.title: Pit Strategy
pitStrategy.info: Average pit stop time across all recorded visits. The decade breakdown shows how tyre compounds, safety-car procedures, and team efficiency have evolved.

fastPit.title: Fastest Pit · Constructor
fastPit.info: Average fastest pit stop per race by constructor. Measures pit-wall execution consistency and mechanical preparation across the full race history.

podNoWin.title: Podiums Without a Win
podNoWin.info: Drivers who have stood on this podium multiple times but never converted to a win. Reveals near-miss specialists and the circuit's competitive ceiling.

lapEvo.title: Lap Time Evolution
lapEvo.info: Fastest lap time recorded each year. Drops reflect car performance leaps; plateaus or increases signal major regulation changes.

sections.standingsInfo: Championship standings after the latest round. Last 5 shows the finishing position of the most recent races, oldest to newest: gold = win, black = podium, red × = retirement.

battle.title: The Title Fight
battle.info: Cumulative championship points, round by round, for the current top 5. A dashed line marks the second driver of a team. The red number is the leader's points advantage over P2.

duel.title: Qualifying H2H
duel.note: Score = sessions ahead · Δ = avg gap
duel.gapTitle: Average gap in the deepest shared session
duel.info: Teammate head-to-head in 2026 qualifying. The score counts sessions where each driver out-qualified the other; Δ is the average time gap in the deepest session both ran, credited to the faster driver.

wall.title: Champions · {from} → {to}
wall.info: Every World Champion since 1950, most recent on the right. ×N counts that driver's titles so far. The red cell is the current season's points leader — the title is still in play. Click a champion to open their profile.

driverDetail.noData: No race data available for this driver.

constructorDetail.noData: No race data available for this constructor.

verdict.title: The Verdict
verdict.info: Career totals, metric by metric. Bars grow from the center axis; the side with the better number keeps full color and scores one point on the tally above. Percentages normalize for career length.

h2h.title: On-Track Head-to-Head
h2h.info: Every Grand Prix both drivers actually started, and who finished ahead. If one retired and the other was classified, the classified driver takes it; double retirements score nothing. The smaller line counts qualifying sessions.
h2h.never: They never shared a grid — different eras.

arc.title: Career Arc
arc.info: Cumulative race wins by career season — both careers start at S1, so drivers from different eras overlay honestly. Gold dots mark championship-winning seasons.

hth.infoTeammates: Seasons in which both drivers raced for the same team — the only years with truly equal machinery. Championship position, points and wins for each.
hth.infoShared: Every season both teams competed in — championship position, points and wins for each.

records.title: Records

records.indexMetaDescription: Who has the most wins, poles, podiums and championships in F1 history — drivers and constructors? Sixteen all-time rankings, updated after every Grand Prix.

privacyPage.metaDescription: How PaddockIntel collects and uses your email address.
privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.s1p: When you subscribe to the PaddockIntel Weekly Digest, we collect your email address and your preferred language (English, Spanish, or Portuguese). We collect nothing else — no name, no tracking cookies tied to your subscription.
privacyPage.s2p: Your email address is used only to send the PaddockIntel Weekly Digest. We do not sell, share, or transfer your email to any third party. We do not use your address for advertising or profiling.
privacyPage.s3p: Subscription records are stored in Supabase (database hosted in the United States). Emails are delivered via Resend (transactional email provider). Both operate under their own privacy policies and data processing agreements.
privacyPage.s4p: Every digest email contains an unsubscribe link at the bottom. Clicking it removes your address immediately and permanently. You can also contact us directly at <mail>info@paddockintel.com</mail>.
privacyPage.s5p: paddockintel.com does not use advertising cookies or third-party analytics trackers. Our hosting provider (Vercel) keeps standard, short-lived server logs (IP address, requested page) needed to operate and secure the service.
privacyPage.s6p: Questions about this policy: <mail>info@paddockintel.com</mail> or via the <about>about page</about>.
